proposals.before: I often wished to debate with commoners on the road and hear merchants speak freely in the markets, so that word might reach your ears and awaken your heart once — even if condemned for seditious speech I would feel no regret.
proposals.after: I often wished to debate with commoners on the road and have merchants criticize in the markets, so that word might reach your ears and awaken your heart once — even if condemned for seditious speech I would feel no regret.
proposals.reason: Chinese 謗於市 means criticize or speak ill in the marketplace; idiomatic 'speak freely' invents a freedom sense absent from 謗 and softens the source.

proposals.before: As for the methods of Guan Yi, they are not the authority of the sage-king;
proposals.after: As for the methods of Yiwu, they are not the authority of the sage-king;
proposals.reason: Chinese 夷吾 is the personal name Yiwu (Guan Zhong); literal English 'Guan Yi' truncates and misrenders the name.

proposals.before: It records his name, condemning how he kept worthy scholars at a distance, favored men of punishment, and conducted himself unlike a true ruler.
proposals.after: It records his name, condemning how he kept worthy scholars at a distance, favored mutilated men, and conducted himself unlike a true ruler.
proposals.reason: 刑人 means mutilated or castrated persons (typically eunuchs), not 'men of punishment'; the condemnation is intimacy with mutilated attendants.

proposals.before: It records his name, condemning how he kept worthy scholars at a distance, was intimate with punishers, and had the conduct of one who is not a ruler.
proposals.after: It records his name, condemning how he kept worthy scholars at a distance, was intimate with mutilated men, and had the conduct of one who is not a ruler.
proposals.reason: 刑人 is 'mutilated men', not 'punishers'; literal English invents the wrong referent class.

proposals.before: Moreover there are those in office not according to their ability, at left and right not the worthy — wicked as the Four Evils, deceitful as Zhao Gao, treacherous as Gong and Xian — why does Your Majesty shrink from not removing them?
proposals.after: Moreover there are those in office not according to their ability, at left and right not the worthy — wicked as the Four Evils, deceitful as Zhao Gao, treacherous as Gong and Xian — why does Your Majesty shrink from removing them?
proposals.reason: Chinese 何憚而不去邪 means 'why shrink from removing them'; the literal's 'shrink from not removing' reverses the sense with a double negative.

proposals.before: Your subject has heard that Yao and Yu as rulers brought all under Heaven to great order because they could employ the Nine Officers, the Four Peaks, and the Twelve Pastors — not missing the right appointment, not duplicating their tasks, not encroaching on their duties; in office only according to ability, at left and right only the worthy; Yuan Kai below though slight yet always raised, the Four Evils in court though strong yet always executed; examining security and danger, clarifying what to take and what to discard.
proposals.after: Your subject has heard that Yao and Yu as rulers brought all under Heaven to great order because they could employ the Nine Officers, the Four Peaks, and the Twelve Pastors — not missing the right appointment, not duplicating their tasks, not encroaching on their duties; in office only according to ability, at left and right only the worthy; the Yuan and Kai below though slight yet always raised, the Four Evils in court though strong yet always executed; examining security and danger, clarifying what to take and what to discard.
proposals.reason: 元凱 denotes the collective Eight Yuan and Eight Kai worthies, not a personal name 'Yuan Kai'.

proposals.before: Formerly Qin's perishing was lost through violent severity;
proposals.after: Formerly Qin's perishing was through violent severity;
proposals.reason: 失於 means 'failed through / was lost by'; 'was lost through' double-marks the loss and obscures the idiom.

proposals.before: If misfortune adds plague upon this, followed by fierce famine — Chen Sheng and Wu Guang did not arise only in Qin, the Red Eyebrows and Yellow Turbans did not arise only in Han; this is why I vent indignation for you, clench my fists, and grieve to the point of weeping blood.
proposals.after: If misfortune adds plague upon this, followed by fierce famine — Chen Sheng and Wu Guang did not arise only in Qin, the Red Eyebrows and Yellow Turbans did not arise only in Han; this is why I vent indignation for you, clutch my wrists, and grieve to the point of weeping blood.
proposals.reason: 扼腕 is the classical gesture of clutching one's wrists in indignation, not clenching fists.

proposals.before: Hearts of benevolence and righteousness are moved below, qi of peace and harmony respond above — therefore disasters do not arise, auspicious omens are preserved and arrive, the four directions reach tranquility, the ten thousand things all succeed.
proposals.after: Hearts of benevolence and righteousness are moved below, qi of peace and harmony respond above — therefore disasters do not arise, auspicious omens arrive in succession, the four directions reach tranquility, and the ten thousand things all succeed.
proposals.reason: 存臻 is the sequential-arrival idiom (荐臻); "are preserved and arrive" invents a preserve sense that obscures the omen phrase.

proposals.before: What your subject earlier called "broad sowing and planting lies in observing food strength."
proposals.after: What your subject earlier called "broad sowing and planting lies in observing the people's capacity to produce food."
proposals.reason: 食力 means productive capacity for food, not an opaque compound food strength; the calque obscures the policy point.

proposals.before: reflecting on the hundred measures' need for correctness — it lies in selecting the myriad offices and personally entrusting them, letting them focus on keeping to their duties;
proposals.after: reflecting on the hundred measures' need for correctness — it lies in selecting the myriad officials and entrusting them, letting them focus on keeping to their duties;
proposals.reason: Chinese 面任之 parallels neighboring 以任之 lines and is almost certainly 而任之 or 以任之; personally is invented from reading 面 as face-to-face.

proposals.before: reflecting on the hundred measures' need for correctness — it lies in selecting the myriad offices and personally entrusting them, letting them focus on keeping to their duties;
proposals.after: reflecting on the hundred measures' need for correctness — it lies in selecting the myriad officials and entrusting them, letting them focus on keeping to their duties;
proposals.reason: Same 面 corruption as the idiomatic line; keep the parallel entrust them wording without inventing personally.

proposals.before: Your subject is not unaware that when words issue disaster responds, when plans are carried out the body is punished — broadly grieving the altars' peril, mourning the living people's regret: how could he bear to temporize with the times' taboos and steal one life of Your Majesty's favor?
proposals.after: Your subject is not unaware that when words issue disaster responds, when plans are carried out the body is punished — broadly grieving the altars' peril, mourning the living people's suffering: how could he bear to temporize with the times' taboos and steal one life of Your Majesty's favor?
proposals.reason: 生人之悔 here means the people's misery or suffering, as the idiomatic already renders, not regret.

decisions.after: I often wished to debate with commoners on the road and hear merchants voice criticism in the markets, so that word might reach your ears and awaken your heart once — even if condemned for seditious speech I would feel no regret.
decisions.reason: 商賈謗於市 pairs with 議於道; 謗 is criticism, not merely speaking freely. The revision preserves that force while supplying a natural English link to the merchants' speech.
夷吾 is Guan Zhong’s given name Yiwu; “Guan Yi” mis-splits and truncates the two-character name present in the Chinese.
In the Spring and Autumn note on 閽弒吳子余祭, 昵刑人 condemns intimacy with mutilated/castrated persons, not “men of punishment.”
刑人 are persons who have undergone mutilating punishment; “punishers” invents the wrong agent class against 昵刑人.
何憚而不去邪 asks why shrink from removing them; “shrink from not removing” reverses the force of 不去.
元凱 paired with 四兇 denotes the collective Eight Yuan and Eight Kai, not a personal name “Yuan Kai.”
失於强暴 is adequately rendered by “was lost through”; dropping “lost” merely smooths style and weakens the mapping of 失, while the awkward doubling with 亡 is not a semantic error.

decisions.after: If misfortune adds plague upon this, followed by fierce famine — Chen Sheng and Wu Guang did not arise only in Qin, the Red Eyebrows and Yellow Turbans did not arise only in Han; this is why I vent indignation for you, clutch my wrist in anguish, and grieve to the point of weeping blood.
decisions.reason: 扼腕 is the classical gesture of clutching one's wrist in indignation; the revision corrects the bodily action and states its emotional force naturally.
休祥存臻 is the omen phrase equivalent to 荐臻 (successive arrival); “are preserved and arrive” invents a preserve sense for 存 that the parallel omen idiom does not support.
視食力, clarified by the following 民勤於食 material, concerns the people’s food-producing capacity; “food strength” is an opaque calque that obscures that policy sense.
Old Tangshu’s parallel and other Xin Tangshu editions read 擇庶官而任之 with the neighboring 以任之 lines; “personally” invents a face-to-face sense from 面, and 庶官 here are officials.
Same parallel as the idiomatic line: authoritative witnesses have 而任之, so literal “personally entrusting” invents meaning from the 面 variant while 庶官 are the officials entrusted.
哀生人之悔, paired with 痛社稷之危 and matching the idiomatic “suffering,” uses 悔 as the people’s misery/calamity, not emotional regret.
